products.name: Nº.8 Bond Intense Moisture Mask
products.shortDescription: A rinse-out bond-building mask that pairs avocado oil and ceramides with Olaplex's patented technology for dry, color-treated hair.
products.fullReview:
Nº.8 Bond Intense Moisture Mask is Olaplex's dedicated moisture step, positioned to sit alongside the brand's better-known bond-repair treatments rather than replace them. The formula is built around Olaplex's patented bond-building chemistry alongside a skincare-inspired ingredient list, so the pitch is moisture and repair in one rinse-out step rather than moisture alone.

The ingredient deck leans on avocado (Persea Gratissima) oil, glycerin, ceramides AP and NP, squalane, sodium hyaluronate, and rose hip seed extract to supply humectant and emollient support, the kind of blend that is typically aimed at dehydrated mid-lengths and ends rather than scalp conditioning. Dimethicone appears high on the ingredient list, which helps explain the smoothing, detangling feel reviewers describe, though it also means regular users of sulfate-free or low-poo routines may want to clarify periodically to avoid buildup.

Application is straightforward: the brand directs users to apply the mask to clean, damp hair from mid-length to ends, work it through, and leave it on for about ten minutes before rinsing, using more or less product depending on hair length and density. The airless pump is designed to help ration product, since the brand markets this as a concentrated, less-is-more formula rather than one to coat the hair in.

For a reader with color-treated hair, the main appeal is that the brand positions No.8 as compatible with color-processed and chemically treated hair without stripping tone, and it is formulated without sulfates or parabens. The trade-off is the fragrance load (including citral, hexyl cinnamal, and limonene) and the silicone content, both of which are worth noting for anyone with a sensitized scalp or a strict no-silicone routine.
pros: Combines Olaplex's bond-building technology with a moisture-focused blend of avocado oil, ceramides, squalane, and hyaluronic acid
Brand directions keep the routine simple: ten-minute leave-on time on clean, damp hair
Airless pump is designed to control dosing so the concentrated formula is not overused
Formulated without sulfates, phthalates, parabens, or gluten and positioned as safe for color-treated hair
cons: Contains dimethicone, a silicone that can build up on fine or low-porosity hair without periodic clarifying
Contains fragrance and fragrance allergens (citral, hexyl cinnamal, limonene) that may not suit fragrance-sensitive scalps
The 3.3 oz size is concentrated but can run out quickly on long, thick, or coarse hair used weekly
products.bestFor: Readers with dry, color-treated, or mechanically damaged hair who want a lightweight rinse-out mask that adds shine and body without a heavy silicone feel.

products.name: Don't Despair, Repair! Deep Conditioning Mask
products.shortDescription: A silicone-free jar mask built on Briogeo's NOVA Complex of rosehip, argan oil, and biotin for dry, color- and chemically-treated hair.
products.fullReview:
Don't Despair, Repair! Deep Conditioning Mask is Briogeo's core weekly treatment, formulated around what the brand calls its NOVA Complex, a blend meant to combine protein and moisture support rather than lean entirely on one or the other. That protein-plus-moisture framing is the main differentiator from a pure moisture mask, and it is why the brand markets this specifically toward hair that has been chemically processed.

The ingredient list is built on brassica alcohol, cetyl alcohol, and stearyl alcohol as the conditioning base, layered with avocado oil, sweet almond oil, rosehip fruit oil, and argan oil for emollience, plus panthenol and biotin along with hydrolyzed wheat, soy, and corn proteins for strength support. The formula is explicitly silicone-free and sulfate-free, which matters for anyone trying to avoid buildup on color-treated hair between salon visits.

Briogeo positions the mask as safe for color-treated, keratin-treated, chemically treated, and relaxed hair, and recommends using it weekly in place of a regular conditioner. The brand also cites its own testing showing hair measured stronger after repeated use, a brand-reported result rather than independent third-party data, so it is worth reading as directional rather than a guaranteed outcome for every hair type.

The jar format is the practical trade-off: unlike a pump mask, a jar means fingers (or a spatula) go in and out of the product repeatedly, which some readers find less hygienic over time, and the floral fragrance is more noticeable than in lighter leave-in formulas. For dry, color-treated hair that is tolerant of a richer, protein-forward conditioner, it remains a reasonable weekly option.
pros: Built on a NOVA Complex blend of rosehip, argan, and avocado oils plus biotin and B-vitamins for a protein-and-moisture balance
Silicone-free and sulfate-free formula, which limits buildup risk on color-treated hair
Brand positions the mask as safe for color-treated, keratin-treated, chemically treated, and relaxed hair
98% naturally derived and formulated without parabens, phthalates, or artificial dyes
cons: Jar packaging means repeated hand or tool contact with the product, which some users find less hygienic than a pump
The floral fragrance is noticeably stronger than in lighter, leave-in style treatments
Brand-reported strength testing is self-reported marketing data rather than independent clinical verification
products.bestFor: Readers with dry, color-treated, or chemically processed hair who want a richer weekly conditioning mask without silicones.

comparisons.title: Olaplex Nº.8 vs. Briogeo Don't Despair, Repair!: Which Mask Fits Dry, Color-Treated Hair?
comparisons.subtitle: A silicone-based bond-moisture mask versus a silicone-free protein-and-moisture mask for color-treated strands
comparisons.winnerReason: For color-treated hair specifically, Briogeo's silicone-free, protein-and-moisture formula is explicitly positioned as safe for color-treated, keratin-treated, and chemically treated hair, which lowers the risk of buildup that can dull color between salon visits compared with the silicone-containing Olaplex formula.
comparisons.verdict: Both masks are reasonable weekly options for dry hair, but they solve slightly different problems. Olaplex Nº.8 is the better fit for readers who want a lightweight, pump-dispensed mask with bond-building chemistry and don't mind a small amount of silicone for slip and shine. Briogeo's Don't Despair, Repair! mask is the stronger pick for readers prioritizing a silicone-free, protein-and-moisture balanced formula explicitly marketed as safe for color-treated and chemically processed hair, accepting a jar format in exchange.
